newsitem.title: USA: Cunanan was witty, charming, vane and dangerous. [CORRECTED 16:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cunanan was witty, charming, vane and dangerous. [CORRECTED 16:10 GMT]

text.p: Witty, intelligent and charming to his friends and lovers, a scheming, narcissistic killer to law officers, Andrew Cunanan has succeeded in gaining the attention he craved.

His life ended 40 blocks away from the spot where eight days earlier he gained international notoriety by allegedly killing Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace outside his mansion in glamourous Miami Beach.

In the days following the murder Cunanan's face stared out from wanted posters, magazine covers and newspaper front-pages across the United States. The most-used photo showed a slighly chubby, olive-skinned visage, wearing wire-rimmed glasses and with short dark hair.
Investigators said he was a master of disguise. He may have resorted to dressing as a woman as he evaded a police manhunt mounted nationwide but focused on south Florida.
Hundreds of tips were phoned in to police, placing him as far apart as local gay bars to near the Canadian border. But the saga ended in a houseboat on a creek off Miami Beach.

A police Special Response Team entered the boat on Wednesday night after a siege lasting several hours. Shortly before dawn Miami Beach police chief Richard Barreto announced a body found inside, an apparent suicide, was Cunanan's.
Cunanan, 27, was also sought in connection with four other murders in April and May, including that of his former homosexual lover. He was described by his own mother as "a high-class prostitute".
Prior to his alleged killing spree, he made his living as gay gigolo in the San Diego area, according to friends and acquaintances.

He had a number of wealthy older patrons, including one who paid him $2,000 aa month, gave him a car and took him on holidays to France and to Broadway shows. He was a habitue of gay video bars and targeted the people he wanted to meet, reports said.

Friends remembered him as witty, charming and gregarious, the life and soul of parties, and spending freely even though he appeared to have limited resources. The only proper job he is known to have had was as a drug store clerk in San Diego.
He spoke several languages and always dressed smartly for his upscale customers.
But acquaintances also said he was socially ambitious, forever name dropping, and craved attention.
He also spun various stories about his life. In some accounts he said he had a wife and child, in others that he was the son of an Israeli millionaire.
In fact his father was a Filipino former U.S. Navy officer turned stockbroker who returned to Manila after some business deals went wrong. His mother lives off welfare in Illinois.
But he led a reasonably affluent life in California as a child and attended the exclusive Bishop's School in San Diego.

He was also open about his sexual orientation at school. Several reports have said he would sit and whistle at the boys in the water polo team as they practised. A widely-circulated photo of him from the high school yearbook shows him striking a seductive pose with the caption "OK nice bod".
His class mates voted him "Least Likely to be Forgotten.
After dropping out of college, he had by 1990 embarked on a career as a gay gigolo in San Diego and San Francisco.
Whether he knew Versace at all remains a mystery. Vanity Fair said they met backstage at the San Francsico Opera in 1990 and Versace made a reference to a previous encounter at Lake Como, Italy.

But as he reached his late 20s, friends said, Cunanan began to lose his looks, got fatter and drank more. He found it harder to find clients and his relationship with his main patron ended. He grew depressed.
In April he told friends he was moving to San Francisco but first has some unfinished business in Minneapolis. They bade farewell to him at a champagne party.

A trail of killings, which police attribute to Cunanan, began. The first victims were Cunanan's former lover, Minneapolis architect David Madson, 33, and another friend from San Diego, former Navy man Jeffrey Trail, 27. Trail's body was found rolled up in a rug in Madson's apartment, beaten to death with a hammer. Madson was found shot dead in the weeds of a lake.
Cunanan is then believed to have travelled to Chicago where he allegedly encountered real estate mogul Lee Miglin, 72. His body was found slashed to death in his garage.
The fourth victim, cemetary caretaker William Reese, was discovered murdered in New Jersey on May 9.
Cunanan them made his way to the gay mecca of Miami Beach, according to police. Almost broke, he is believed to have stayed at the rundown Normandy Hotel and pawned a gold coin.

On the morning of July 15 (corrects from July 13), a lone gunman shot dead Versace as he strolled home along Ocean Drive after buying magazines at a local cafe. The final chapter of Cunanan's life began.
